scene.label: Act 2, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Another room in Leonato's house.

lines.text: It is so; the Count Claudio shall marry the daughter of Leonato.
lines.plainText: It is so the Count Claudio shall marry the daughter of Leonato

lines.text: Yea, my lord; but I can cross it.
lines.plainText: Yea my lord but I can cross it

lines.text: Any bar, any cross, any impediment will be medicinable to me: I am sick in displeasure to him, and whatsoever comes athwart his affection ranges evenly with mine. How canst thou cross this marriage?
lines.plainText: Any bar any cross any impediment will be medicinable to me I am sick in displeasure to him and whatsoever comes athwart his affection ranges evenly with mine How canst thou cross this marriage

lines.text: Not honestly, my lord; but so covertly that no dishonesty shall appear in me.
lines.plainText: Not honestly my lord but so covertly that no dishonesty shall appear in me

lines.text: I think I told your lordship, a year since, how much I am in the favour of Margaret, the waiting gentlewoman to Hero.
lines.plainText: I think I told your lordship a year since how much I am in the favour of Margaret the waiting gentlewoman to Hero

lines.text: I can, at any unseasonable instant of the night, appoint her to look out at her lady's chamber window.
lines.plainText: I can at any unseasonable instant of the night appoint her to look out at her lady's chamber window

lines.text: What life is in that, to be the death of this marriage?
lines.plainText: What life is in that to be the death of this marriage

lines.text: The poison of that lies in you to temper. Go you to the Prince your brother; spare not to tell him, that he hath wronged his honour in marrying the renowned Claudio,—whose estimation do you mightily hold up,—to a contaminated stale, such a one as Hero.
lines.plainText: The poison of that lies in you to temper Go you to the Prince your brother spare not to tell him that he hath wronged his honour in marrying the renowned Claudiowhose estimation do you mightily hold upto a contaminated stale such a one as Hero

lines.text: What proof shall I make of that?
lines.plainText: What proof shall I make of that

lines.text: Proof enough to misuse the Prince, to vex Claudio, to undo Hero, and kill Leonato. Look you for any other issue?
lines.plainText: Proof enough to misuse the Prince to vex Claudio to undo Hero and kill Leonato Look you for any other issue

lines.text: Only to despite them, I will endeavour anything.
lines.plainText: Only to despite them I will endeavour anything

lines.text: Go then; find me a meet hour to draw Don Pedro and the Count Claudio alone: tell them that you know that Hero loves me; intend a kind of zeal both to the Prince and Claudio, as—in love of your brother's honour, who hath made this match, and his friend's reputation, who is thus like to be cozened with the semblance of a maid,—that you have discovered thus. They will scarcely believe this without trial: offer them instances, which shall bear no less likelihood than to see me at her chamber window, hear me call Margaret Hero, hear Margaret term me Claudio; and bring them to see this the very night before the intended wedding: for in the meantime I will so fashion the matter that Hero shall be absent; and there shall appear such seeming truth of Hero's disloyalty, that jealousy shall be called assurance, and all the preparation overthrown.
lines.plainText: Go then find me a meet hour to draw Don Pedro and the Count Claudio alone tell them that you know that Hero loves me intend a kind of zeal both to the Prince and Claudio asin love of your brother's honour who hath made this match and his friend's reputation who is thus like to be cozened with the semblance of a maidthat you have discovered thus They will scarcely believe this without trial offer them instances which shall bear no less likelihood than to see me at her chamber window hear me call Margaret Hero hear Margaret term me Claudio and bring them to see this the very night before the intended wedding for in the meantime I will so fashion the matter that Hero shall be absent and there shall appear such seeming truth of Hero's disloyalty that jealousy shall be called assurance and all the preparation overthrown

lines.text: Grow this to what adverse issue it can, I will put it in practice. Be cunning in the working this, and thy fee is a thousand ducats.
lines.plainText: Grow this to what adverse issue it can I will put it in practice Be cunning in the working this and thy fee is a thousand ducats

lines.text: Be you constant in the accusation, and my cunning shall not shame me.
lines.plainText: Be you constant in the accusation and my cunning shall not shame me

lines.text: I will presently go learn their day of marriage.
lines.plainText: I will presently go learn their day of marriage
